There is a drop down in Steam to show only games you can install in Linux. Quite a few games are supported and its improving slowly. Many games will require Wine to run.

Search for the name of a game plus wine and you'll come to a WineHQ page. For example, here is Fallout 3:

https://appdb.winehq.org/objectManager.php?sClass=version&iId=14322

It has a rating of Gold which means it should run pretty much as it would on Windows. These pages also include a lot of user commentary on issues they've run into, solutions, etc.

The core issue is that games designed using the DirectX library will be harder to run in Linux. If the game uses OpenGL or has an OpenGL mode it will typically run in Wine without problems. Of course, many big games are Windows exclusive and use DirectX. There is also typically a delay where DirectX 12 will come out and only run on Windows 10. It will probably be 2-3 years before DirectX 12 functionality is supported at all in Wine.

For decades now one of the largest road blocks for Linux as a desktop has been people who want to play all their games. If game developers dropped DirectX or people created better and timely support for DirectX in Linux I am completely confident that Windows would be dead by now. Usually people install Linux, everything is great but they want games, so they dual boot Windows, then they just end up never using Linux since its a hassle to have to restart to access your games and Windows can do the same things Linux does for the most part.
